Subject: Redwood responses: DPF mapping + DPA annex (Xenvera RFI)

Elena / Paul —

Attached are our answered rows (redwood_dpf_mapping.csv) and the current DPA annex extract (redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf). Highlights:

- Data residency: Hosted API (default) stores customer-provided content in the region requested at provisioning time. For dedicated/private deployments we support VPC/on-prem options; when required we can restrict inference and storage to specific cloud regions or on-prem clusters.

- Cross-border transfers: We support SCC-based transfer mechanisms and maintain a DPA annex that enumerates subprocessors and transfer safeguards (Section 3 of the annex). We also provide documented mapping for any customer-configured data flows.

- KMS/key custody: Customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or external HSM via KMIP). For customer-managed keys we provide envelope encryption at the storage layer; key material never leaves the KMS/HSM boundary. Evidence attached: KMS_architecture_diagram excerpt (see annex).

- Logs & retention: Token-level logs for debugging are retained for 30 days by default in hosted; audit logs (access, configuration changes) are retained for 1 year in our control plane. Longer retention is available as an add-on. Production tenants can opt-in to export logs to customer S3 for long-term archival.

Attachments included: redwood_dpf_mapping.csv (mapping of each RFI row to evidence), redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (annotated), sample_kms_integration.json (redacted snippet).

Please review and call out any items you want expanded. If you prefer an encrypted ZIP bundle, say the word and we'll produce one.

Regards,
Alex

Attachment stubs: redwood_dpf_mapping.csv, redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf, sample_kms_integration.json

Alex —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the mapping. A few clarifying questions from our security review:

1) For customer-managed KMS, can you confirm whether encryption-in-transit keys are separate from disk-encryption keys, and whether those keys are rotated automatically? We need the rotation cadence and whether rotations require application downtime.

2) Subprocessors: can you provide the current list of hyperscaler and infra subprocessors with country of processing? The annex covers general categories but our procurement team requires a table of vendor, service, country.

3) Data residency enforcement: for hosted tenants, what prevents data from being backed up to a different region during DR drills? Any guardrails we can reference?

If possible, we prefer a short (one-page) technical memo addressing the three bullets above. That will speed our legal sign-off.

Paul Trask
